Article Title: Vansh Bedi reported fixing approach during Delhi Premier League 3; DDCA seeks BCCI intervention
Article Text:

New Delhi:

Controversy has gripped the recently concluded season of the Delhi Premier League (DPL) with Vansh Bedi, who played for Central Delhi Kings, reporting a "fixing approach" by a cricketer from a neighbouring state. It has learnt that the young wicketkeeper-batter flagged the approach to the Anti-Corruption Wing, which was later document as well."Vansh Bedi promptly reported a corrupt approach to the Anti-Corruption wing from a player from Uttar Pradesh, who was also playing a T20 league in the state. We have attached SLOs with every team this year and all our arrangements have been watertight," said DDCA Secretary Ashok Sharma.The Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) has written to the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) seeking advice on the matter, and how to approach the fixing claims stemming from a sting operation conducted by Tehelka."We have written to the BCCI and will await their guidance," added the DDCA secretary.TimesofIndia.com has reached out to BCCI Secretary Devajit Saikia for a comment and the story will be updated moment they respond. Insiders in the Delhi cricket corridors feel there is more than meets the eye but DDCA officials will act after receiving guidance from the Indian cricket board.Central Delhi Kings were the runners-up this season, losing to South Delhi Superstarz in the title clash. Prior to this edition, Bedi played for Purani Dilli 6 and also had a stint with Chennai Super Kings in the Indian Premier League.
Article Summary: Vansh Bedi, who played for Central Delhi Kings, reported a "fixing approach" by a cricketer from a neighbouring state. The Delhi and District Cricket Association (DDCA) has written to the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) seeking advice on the matter.

Article Title: ‘Focus on possible medals’: India rowing coach defends last-minute Asian Games changes
Article Text:
Asian Games 2026 (Reuters Photo)

There is disenchantment among rowers at the Asian Games over last-minute changes in competition entries, but the head coach and the president of the Rowing Federation of India have said the decisions were made due to a curtailed programme and with the best chances of winning “big medals” in mind.“Due to the shortened regatta programme, I as the chief coach have made the decision to focus on possible medals, not individual comfort of athletes,” coach Antony Patterson told TOI in a text message on Monday.Balaji Maradapa, the RFI president, highlighted the difficult conditions due to heavy rain and the need to adapt because of the change in schedule.“Originally it was four plus one day of races. Now it is just two days and four sessions of races each day. How can you be doubling,” Balaji said, referring to rowers competing in two aligned events.For instance, a team of athletes taking part in doubles scull and pair, or two single scullers, might be combined to form a quadruple scull.
Article Summary: There is disenchantment among rowers at the Asian Games over last-minute changes in competition entries. The head coach and the president of the Rowing Federation of India have said the decisions were made due to a curtailed programme and with the best chances of winning "big medals" in mind.

Article Title: 163 years before India-Japan T20I, cricket’s first match in Japan had revolvers behind the stumps
Article Text:
India vs Japan T20I Photo/BCCI

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In the land of baseball, cricket is all set to score on Tuesday when India and Japan celebrate 75 years of diplomatic ties with a T20 International for the Suzuki Cup at the petite Sano International Cricket Ground, about 80 km from Tokyo.It’s a historic occasion. But neither side is likely to be as tense and twitchy as those who played the first-ever cricket match in the Land of the Rising Sun in the summer of 1863. In that game, some players carried unusual protective gear: revolvers. The wicketkeeper would place his piece behind the stumps. The ground was guarded ‘by a small force armed with rifles’.Few cricket matches have been more nerve-wracking.Two British sides, the Navy and the Shore Team, the latter consisting of expatriates in Japan, faced off in the port town of Yokohama. Players were nervous because an attack from the sharp-sworded samurai was feared.Details of the strange but true incident came to light in 2012 following the efforts of dogged amateur British historian Mike Galbraith, who subsequently wrote about it in The Japan Times.While researching sports in Japan, Galbraith spotted the Wisden obituary of a British admiral, Sir Harry Rawson.The tribute said that he had played in the first cricket game in Japan. Further research led to an article in London-based ‘Cricket’ magazine written by James Campbell Fraser, the Shore Team’s skipper and a former Harrow student.In his article, Galbraith quoted Fraser: “It was a most novel sensation for the wicket-keeper, as he carried his revolver backwards and forwards from wicket to wicket and placed it behind the stumps.”Galbraith had earlier calculated that the match was played towards the end of June. However, he later discovered a naval officer’s diary, which led him to conclude that the game occurred over a month earlier.“The evidence shows that the match was played on or around May 12, 1863,” he said in an email response last week.In Japanese history, these were the final years of the shogunate, a period ruled by hereditary military governors. An incident in which bodyguards of a Japanese warlord had killed an English merchant had caused rage and bitterness. All foreigners were asked to leave the country by the end of June 1863.Galbraith said that the marines were sent to provide security cover for the expatriates and were stationed on the ships. However, no samurai attack occurred that day or later.The Navy team won. Fraser’s Shore men ‘got a jolly good lickin’.Five years later, the first cricket club in Japan was set up by Scottish tea merchant J P Mollison in Yokohama. But the sport didn’t take off; baseball did.Of late, though, cricket is finding its feet. According to the Japanese Cricket Association website, there are 7,300 players and about 14,000 annual participants in the Land of the Rising Sun.Japan’s greatest moment in the willow game came when the women’s team claimed bronze at the 2010 Asian Games.
Article Summary: India and Japan celebrate 75 years of diplomatic ties with a T20 International for the Suzuki Cup at the petite Sano International Cricket Ground, about 80 km from Tokyo. Two British sides, the Navy and the Shore Team, the latter consisting of expatriates in Japan, faced off in the port town of Yokohama. Players were nervous because an attack from the sharp-sworded samurai was feared.

Article Title: 'Serve and volley is completely fading': Rajeev Ram's blunt take on modern tennis
Article Text:
Rajeev Ram. (Photo by Paul Kane/Getty Images)

Tennis is a demanding sport. How were you able to keep going until 42?

How fitting was it to finish your career at the US Open?

Is the art of

serve and volley

fading?

Your take on mixed doubles being played a week before the US Open?

Bengaluru: Six-time Grand Slam champion across doubles and mixed doubles, Rajeev Ram, 42, called time on his career at the US Open earlier this month. The former doubles world No. 1 spoke to TOI about his career, the transition to doubles and the journey that followed. Excerpts...I was always going to play until my body would allow me to do it. More than the sport, the travel got really hard, changing time zones all the time. You have to be in peak physical shape to play. And I found that as I got older, it became harder to do that.I don’t think I could have written it better. Maybe if I had won the US Open doubles again, it would have been (great). But to make the semis along with my longtime doubles partner (Salisbury), have my coaches, friends and family there, I don’t think I could have thought of a better way to end my career.It’s completely fading. The technology, the strings, the rackets, the courts, the balls, nothing is conducive to that style of tennis. Basically, it feels there’s no court, or very few courts and conditions in the world, that are conducive to that style.If it was there, you would see it. You just don’t see it at the top of the game, or at any level.It’s a shame because I think that style really added contrast, which, for me, was the beautiful part of tennis when you had two players playing a different style against each other.I was happy with the fact that the US Open is trying to innovate. But I didn’t feel they included enough of the doubles players and people who specialise in that event to warrant it being called a Grand Slam. They gave a Grand Slam-winning trophy to the winner, but they didn’t include everybody that, I think, was at the best level, at the top of the game.
Article Summary: Rajeev Ram is a six-time Grand Slam champion across doubles and mixed doubles. The 42-year-old called time on his career at the US Open earlier this month. Ram spoke to TOI about his career, the transition to doubles and the journey that followed.

Article Title: Chetan Bhatt suffers heartbreak, loses Asian Games bronze medal to Chinese Taipei on Senshu
Article Text:
Chetan Bhatt misses bronze after 1-1 draw, loses Kumite playoff to Chinese Taipei on Senshu (Reuters)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India's Chetan Bhatt suffered heartbreak at the Asian Games 2026 after losing the men's Kumite 84kg bronze medal playoff to Chinese Taipei's Meng-yu Chung on Tuesday.The bout at the Toyohashi Gymnasium ended 1-1 after regulation time, but Chung walked away with the bronze medal on the basis of Senshu, which is awarded to the athlete who scores the first point without conceding one beforehand.Both karatekas managed one Yuko each during the contest, but Chung had struck first and that proved decisive when the scores remained level at the end. Under karate's Senshu rule, the athlete who scores the first uncontested point is declared the winner in a tied bout.Bhatt had reached the bronze medal playoff after a difficult semifinal against Jordan's Mohammad Aljafari. The Indian went down 0-8 to Aljafari, missing out on a place in the gold medal contest and having to settle for a shot at bronze.However, Bhatt could not convert that opportunity as Chung held his nerve in a closely fought playoff. The narrow defeat meant India missed out on another medal in karate at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games.Elsewhere, India's Jay Meena picked up a notable win in soft tennis, defeating Pakistan's Arain Hussain in their Group D clash. Jay produced a dominant 4-0 victory, winning the four sets 4-2, 4-0, 4-2, 4-0.India's Aadhya Tiwari, meanwhile, suffered a 1-4 defeat to Thailand's Alisha Ziegler in the women's singles competition.Aadhya won the opening set 4-1 but Ziegler fought back to take the next four sets 4-0, 4-0, 2-4, 4-6.With only the group winners advancing to the quarterfinals, Aadhya's qualification hopes now depend on her result against Pakistan's Kainaat Shallwani and the outcome of Shallwani's match against Ziegler.India also suffered another setback in men's sepaktakraw. The Indian team lost 0-2 to Malaysia in their second Group B contest, going down 9-15, 12-15. The defeat leaves India's campaign hanging by a thread, with the Philippines their final group-stage opponent on Wednesday.India had earlier lost their opening Group B match 1-2 to Japan on Monday.
Article Summary: Chetan Bhatt loses men's Kumite 84kg bronze medal playoff to Chinese Taipei's Meng-yu Chung. The bout ended 1-1 after regulation time, but Chung won on Senshu. Under karate's Senshu rule, the athlete who scores the first uncontested point is declared the winner in a tied bout.

Article Title: Asian Games 2026: Typhoon Dujuan threatens Aichi-Nagoya as organisers postpone equestrian event
Article Text:
L-R: Asian Games football match; a flooded area following heavy rain as Typhoon Dujuan approaches Japan. (Reuters Photos)

Equestrian event postponed as storm approaches

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A powerful typhoon approaching Japan's Pacific coast has raised concerns over possible disruption to the Asian Games 2026, with organisers taking a precautionary step by postponing the equestrian eventing competition as Typhoon Dujuan threatens to bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of the country.The Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) warned that conditions could deteriorate rapidly as Dujuan moves towards eastern Japan. The storm was expected to pass near the Boso Peninsula in Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Monday evening, while heavy rain could continue through Tuesday.The agency also warned of the possibility of linear rainbands over parts of the Kanto-Koshin and Tokai regions. Such systems can produce intense rainfall over a concentrated area for several hours, increasing the risk of flash floods and landslides.Although the Aichi-Nagoya Games venues had not experienced significant adverse weather on Monday morning, organisers postponed the equestrian eventing competition from Monday to Tuesday as a precaution. The change was also linked to concerns over heavy rain and delays in preparing the riding arena.The wider weather situation has already affected transport in Japan, with parts of highways closed. Authorities have also warned of landslide and flooding risks in areas expected to receive the heaviest rain.For the Asian Games , the immediate impact remains focused on weather-sensitive outdoor events and transportation, while organisers continue monitoring conditions. Tokyo, which is hosting some Asian Games competitions, is also expected to experience the storm's effects.
Article Summary: Typhoon Dujuan threatens to bring heavy rain and strong winds to parts of Japan. The storm was expected to pass near the Boso Peninsula in Chiba Prefecture, east of Tokyo, on Monday evening. Heavy rain could continue through Tuesday, according to the Japan Meteorological Agency.

Article Title: Typhoon Dujuan forces India to miss training ahead of Japan T20I; Shreyas Iyer says ‘don’t know conditions’
Article Text:
India captain Shreyas Iyer (Video grab)

Typhoon disrupts India's preparations

Iyer excited despite unfamiliar conditions

Poll Vote & Share your view What aspect of the match are you most excited about? India's historic participation Japan's performance The atmosphere and crowd Player performances 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: India’s preparations for their historic T20 International against Japan were disrupted by rain and stormy conditions on Monday, with Typhoon Dujuan approaching eastern Japan and preventing the Shreyas Iyer-led side from training on the eve of the landmark fixture.The powerful typhoon was moving towards Japan’s Pacific coast, bringing torrential rain, strong winds and an increased risk of landslides across the Kanto region, which includes Tokyo and surrounding areas. The Japan Meteorological Agency warned that conditions could deteriorate rapidly as the storm moved closer to the region.The India squad is based in Japan ahead of Tuesday’s match at the Sano International Cricket Ground in Tochigi Prefecture. The fixture, called the Suzuki Cup, marks the first meeting between India and Japan in men’s international cricket and has been organised as part of celebrations marking 75 years of India-Japan diplomatic relations.Heavy rain had already lashed parts of eastern Japan, with the Izu Islands and areas along the Pacific coast recording more than 300 mm of rainfall since Saturday. The weather agency warned that rainfall could intensify as Dujuan approached the Kanto region, while authorities also cautioned about the possibility of linear rain bands capable of triggering flash floods.The weather disruption has also affected the ongoing Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, with organisers postponing the equestrian eventing competition as a precaution against the approaching storm.For India, the loss of the eve-of-match training session means the players will head into a first-ever international encounter with Japan without a final opportunity to familiarise themselves with the local conditions.That could be particularly relevant given that even captain Iyer admitted the Indian side has limited knowledge of the playing conditions and wicket.Speaking ahead of the match, Iyer described his experience in Japan so far as "beautiful" and praised the hospitality he and his teammates had received."It is beautiful. I mean, the time we landed, we saw the people very cordial, generous, and helpful in nature, which we see at back at home as well. The hospitality is brilliant, and yeah, I mean, it is too early to talk about it, but I'm sure that I've heard special things from people about Japan as a country and Tokyo as a city as well, so looking forward to explore more," Iyer said in a video shared by BCCI The India captain acknowledged the unfamiliarity surrounding the contest."It is going to be a thrilling and exciting match for us. This is the first time we would be playing Japan, and do not know much about the conditions, the wicket, but looking forward to have a great match," he added.The match also serves as India's final preparation before their Asian Games campaign, which begins on September 28 with a quarterfinal. India enter the fixture as the reigning T20 World Cup champions, while Japan are ranked 41st in the format. BCCI has confirmed the Japan match as part of India's build-up to the Asian Games.For Japan, meanwhile, the occasion represents a major milestone. The hosts will face one of the biggest names in international cricket on home soil, with Japan captain Kendel Kadowaki-Fleming insisting his side are not merely there to celebrate the occasion but to demonstrate what they can do.
Article Summary: Typhoon disrupts India's preparations for historic T20 International against Japan. Typhoon Dujuan approaching eastern Japan and preventing the Shreyas Iyer- led side from training on the eve of the landmark fixture. The fixture, called the Suzuki Cup, marks the first meeting between India and Japan in men’s international cricket.

For an athlete whose rise has been built on performances rather than publicity, Rinku Singh is now taking a big step towards building a global brand. The India cricketer has signed with EMW Global for international talent representation, becoming the agency's first Indian client as it expands into one of the world's fastest-growing sports markets.Founded by Michael Rocha Keys, EMW Global has established its presence across emerging markets with a vision of helping talent grow internationally while connecting brands with local audiences.In a conversation with select media, Keys explained why India is central to the agency's next phase, what made Rinku stand out beyond his cricketing credentials, and how the partnership aims to develop his commercial profile through long-term brand partnerships and cross-sport collaborations in key international markets.Apart from India being an incredible country, with an incredible culture, and a love and a passion for sports, it's also a country which is quite close to my heart. The diaspora of Indians around the world is especially present here in London. Quite apart from my passion for the food and the people.Having made many visits more recently for my best friend's wedding, I do believe that as a market, they have been growing and developing and internationalising, and I think now is the perfect time for EMW to come into the market and to be able to get a foothold.Firstly, with one of the local stars of the sport, and then gradually, slowly but surely helping Rinku to grow his international brand, but also helping to bring lots of international opportunities from different diverse sports into the Indian market.The fans are amazing. We saw around the World Cup all of the different fan groups supporting many different national teams, whether they be Argentina or Brazil, and you can just see the growth of the market. It's exponential.You can see that also by the fact that the Brazilian national team are due to play against India very soon in a football match in India.The market is developing rapidly, we want to be involved, we want to add value, we want to grow together with that upwards trend, and we're very excited by that.First and foremost, he's a character. I think we want to work with people that not just are sports stars, but also, in their own right, characters. They have an appetite for international growth, success both on the pitch and off the pitch, and I think Rinku embodies all of those aspects and those passions.For us, it's a pleasure to work together with him and to grow together with him, because athletes come in all different shapes and sizes.The most important thing is to have success in one's respective sport, but then to be able to build that success off the pitch, or off the court, or off the field into one's respective passions is definitely a match made in heaven for us, and it will really help us to grow and build his international brand.The short answer is yes. In the near to medium future, we will be looking at adding to the roster. However, in the near future, we want to be focusing on Rinku as our first client in the market to be able to help to build and grow and show the market what we can do. First, the priority will be on Rinku, and then in the medium term, sometime probably in the second half of next year, we'll be looking to likely work with other athletes.At the moment, the immediate priority is our friend Rinku.Success can be viewed in many different ways, but if you were to look at success from two main perspectives, one being commercially, from brand partnerships, and the other being from growth of Rinku's brand in international and other priority markets.As an agency, we're going to be looking to help him develop across both those spaces. Building out his brand partnerships, not just in India, but in other key markets, in long-term, committed brands that he also has an interest in.And partnering with other athletes across different markets to help build his brand in those strategic regions, whether it be across media, whether it be across content, whether it be cross-collaborations, like we've been doing a lot here in the UK with David James.The idea will be to help build Rinku's brand through commercial brand partnerships, but also talent partnerships and content collaborations with other top-level athletes in key sports and key regions.Having sporting accolades and being a top-level athlete in one's respective sport will only take you so far. I think one needs to have a mindset out of sports to be able to want to grow one's brand into the international markets, into other industries outside of sport.Rinku's openness and his passion to build his brand outside of India and outside of just the cricket space is definitely what attracted us to want to work with him on an international basis.We are positioning ourselves as the world's local agency, specialising in emerging markets. We have offices across Asia, in Latin America, in Europe, and we'll also soon be expanding offices into South Africa, as well as the US in the coming years.The most important thing to help build Rinku's brand, which will be a process, is understanding his passions outside of cricket, and how we can tap into the diaspora of fans around the world who follow him in the emerging and established markets through partnerships with talent from different sports, whether it be basketball, football or baseball.There are so many different collaboration opportunities, and it's important to not forget that the world looks at India and sees the huge potential. Rinku provides that opportunity as a gateway for not just brands, but other athletes that want to build their brand locally, and at the same time can help Rinku build his brand globally.There really is an amazing crossover opportunity, both ways.I think that's more of a strategic question, and as we've just launched in the market, it's definitely a cause for consideration.Many international sports have come, some successfully, some not so successfully, and tried to launch within the Indian market. As we develop and grow in the market, we'll get an understanding of the challenges around that.Right now we're focused on launching and making sure that we can put the best possible plan in place for Rinku, both from a national and international perspective. Then we can start thinking about what the market holds in terms of other sports.Everyone has a different personality. My personality is different, Rinku's personality is different. Everyone has a different personality and a different way of communicating. Just because people don't say a lot doesn't mean they don't have a lot to say.In front of the media, people have one personality, and in the dressing room, they have another.I don't think quantity is important. I think quality is important. Actions speak louder than words.When you have someone like Rinku, who might not have a lot of things to say in front of the media, I can assure you that when we're sat in meetings, planning projects and doing partnerships with brands, that is not the case.He's very proactive in the way he approaches partnerships, whether it's a brand partnership or an athlete partnership and crossover content, to make sure it's going to be very successful. I don't believe that will be an issue whatsoever.
Article Summary: Rinku Singh has signed with EMW Global for international talent representation. He is the agency's first Indian client as it expands into one of the world's fastest-growing sports markets. Rinku joins an impressive stable of other star athletes like Olivier Giroud and Peter Cech. The partnership aims to develop his commercial profile through long-term brand partnerships.

India's swimmers had another disappointing day at the Asian Games on Monday, with two-time Olympian Srihari Nataraj finishing 10th in the men's 50m backstroke final, while Vedaant Madhavan, son of actor R Madhavan, missed out on the men's 4x200m freestyle relay final.Swimming events at the Asian Games 2026 are being held at the Tokyo Aquatics Centre in Tokyo.Nataraj clocked 25.52 seconds in the final to finish last, slower than his 25.37-second effort in the heats earlier in the day.The 25-year-old had qualified for the final after clocking 25.37 seconds, the same time as Iran's Homer Abbasi, to finish third in his heat and joint ninth overall.Competing in his third Asian Games, Nataraj has a personal best of 25.18 seconds in the event, which he set in Belgrade in June 2021.China's Jiayu Xu won the gold medal and set a new Asian Games record with a time of 24.04 seconds. He broke the previous mark of 24.28 seconds set by Japan's Junya Koga at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon.Rishabh Das, who finished sixth in the men's 100m backstroke on Sunday, narrowly missed the 50m backstroke final. He clocked 25.41 seconds and finished 11th overall.In the men's 50m freestyle, Akash Mani and Geetesh Shah also failed to progress beyond the heats.Akash finished 26th overall after clocking a personal best of 23.43 seconds to top his heat, while Geetesh was 28th overall with a time of 23.57 seconds.South Korea's Youngbeom Kim set a new Asian Games record in the event with a time of 21.71 seconds.Danush Suresh also missed the men's 100m backstroke final after finishing eighth in his heat and 22nd overall in 1:03.46.In the men's 4x200m freestyle relay, Sajan Prakash, Dhakshan Shashikumar, Vedaant Madhavan and Aneesh Sunil failed to qualify for the final. The Indian quartet finished ninth among 13 teams with a time of 7:24.32.After the qualifying round, Vedaant shared a note on his Instagram Story: "Missed finals by 0.2 and best Indian by 0.5, 200 free day after."Vedaant will compete in two more events, the 200m freestyle (September 23) and the 200m backstroke (September 25).R. Madhavan reshared Vedaant's story with a 'gratitude' emoticon.India's wait for a swimming medal at the Asian Games continues. The country's last medal in the sport came at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon, where Sandeep Sejwal won bronze in the men's 50m breaststroke.
Article Summary: Two-time Olympian Srihari Nataraj finishes 10th in men's 50m backstroke final. Vedaant Madhavan misses out on men's 4x200m freestyle relay final. India's last swimming medal came at the 2014 Asian Games in Incheon. China's Jiayu Xu won gold medal and set new Asian Games record.

NAGOYA: At the send-off ceremony for the Indian contingent, Hockey India president Dilip Tirkey had sought to put the jersey controversy to rest.“For the Games, the team will wear blue. That’s the primary colour. There’s no confusion, everything is clear,” he had said. But when the Indian men and women take the field against Indonesia and Uzbekistan, respectively, the primary colour may well be white.In the build-up to the FIH World Cup, the Indian teams’ jerseys had come in for sharp criticism after they moved away from the iconic blue and opted for saffron. The shorts and skirts are also in a lighter shade of blue. The second-choice kit is saffron.“All kits for the Asian Games are routed through the IOA and, by the president’s admission, blue was the colour suggested by Hockey India. But the shade of blue and how it is used is up for debate,” a source said.The choice of colour reportedly did not go down well with Tirkey, prompting an effort to get new kits made.“Given how controversy-plagued Hockey India has been over the past few months, the president does not want the focus to shift away from the teams. That’s why he tried very hard to get new sets of jerseys. But given that they have to come through the sponsors, and the women’s team left soon after the send-off, it was always going to be a race against time,” the source said.
Article Summary: The Indian teams' jerseys had come in for sharp criticism after they moved away from the iconic blue and opted for saffron. Article Title: 'Babar Azam struggles to handle captaincy': Waqar Younis warns 'we are losing a player'

Babar still waiting for Test century

Former Pakistan captain Waqar Younis believes the decision to hand Babar Azam the Test captaincy again could be hurting the batter's performances, arguing that the team risks “losing a player” by placing the leadership burden on him.Waqar, who has served in several coaching roles with the Pakistan men's team, said Babar is a technically accomplished batter but appears to struggle when the additional responsibility of captaincy comes his way. He also suggested that Babar's inability to fully back his teammates under pressure makes the role unfair to both the players and the captain himself.“I have seen him as a player. Technically, a very sound player. Very complete and elegant player. As a player, I don't personally see anything wrong with him. But I think with the captaincy pressure, he takes a little too much on himself. Whenever he takes this responsibility or is given a responsibility, I don't think he performs that well,” said Waqar during an event.“So I think we are losing a player if we are going to give him this responsibility because he struggles to handle that.You have to be strong as a person, and you have to be really out there and back your players. If you cannot back your players, it's unfair to the players and the job,” he added.Waqar's remarks came shortly after Pakistan endured a 3-0 defeat against England in the three-Test series.The series was overshadowed by a major shake-up within the Pakistan camp. After Pakistan fell 0-2 behind, the Pakistan Cricket Board sent seven players and two coaches back home before the final Test.Babar also found himself at the centre of criticism after revealing ahead of the third Test that he had not been consulted by the board, headed by Mohsin Naqvi, over the decisions.The comment drew criticism from former Pakistan captain Wasim Akram , who questioned Babar for not standing by his team.Babar had returned to the Test captaincy earlier this year after Shan Masood was removed from the position following Pakistan's 2-0 series defeat against Bangladesh.Babar's recent struggles with the bat have added another layer to the debate surrounding his leadership role.The 31-year-old has now gone almost four years without a Test century. His most recent hundred in the format came against New Zealand in December 2022.He came close to ending the drought against the West Indies and again in the third and final Test against England, but missed out on both occasions after being dismissed.Pakistan's recent results have also left them ninth in the World Test Championship standings with four points. The team were further penalised by an 11-point deduction for a slow over-rate in the third Test at Edgbaston in Birmingham.

Pakistan women won the bronze medal at the Asian Games after beating Bangladesh by 31 runs in the third-place clash at the Korogi Sports Park on Tuesday.It was a strong all-round performance from Pakistan, who defended 145 after restricting Bangladesh to 114 in 20 overs.The win also helped Pakistan avenge their bronze-medal playoff defeat to Bangladesh at the 2023 Hangzhou Asian Games.Captain Fatima Sana once again played a key role for Pakistan.After Pakistan lost wickets regularly in the middle overs, Sana scored a crucial 45 off 30 balls to help her team post a competitive total.Gull Feroza also made a valuable contribution with 31 off 23 balls, while Aliya Riaz scored 25 off 22 deliveries.Bangladesh had earlier made a strong comeback with the ball. Nahida Akter, Shorna Akter and Ritu Moni picked up two wickets each as Pakistan slipped from 46/0 to 67/5.But Sana and Riaz changed the game with a 67-run partnership for the sixth wicket.The partnership helped Pakistan recover and finish on 145/8.Bangladesh's chase got off to a poor start as they lost three wickets for just 20 runs in 4.1 overs.Nigar Sultana and Sharmin Akhter then tried to rebuild the innings.The pair added 47 runs for the fourth wicket and gave Bangladesh some hope.However, the required run rate kept increasing.Nigar was eventually dismissed for 25 off 30 balls in the 14th over, leaving Bangladesh in deeper trouble.Sharmin remained unbeaten on 46 off 45 balls but struggled to find enough support from the other end.Off-spinner Umm-e-Hani was the star with the ball for Pakistan.She picked up three wickets for just 10 runs and played a key role in Bangladesh's collapse.Hani took two of Bangladesh's first three wickets, removing Juairiya Ferdous and Sobhana Mostary.After Nigar's dismissal, Bangladesh struggled to keep the scoreboard moving. Chennai: Mahendra Singh Dhoni ’s pinnacle as India captain was the 2011 World Cup triumph, and Zaheer Khan was one of that campaign’s unsung heroes. His joint-highest tally of 21 wickets in the tournament, alongside Pakistan skipper Shahid Afridi, and his opening spell of 5-3-6-1 in the final against Sri Lanka at the Wankhede are not celebrated as much as some of the other performances from that campaign.Now, as Dhoni enters the final chapter of his playing career, he has turned to his trusted lieutenant as coach of Chennai Super Kings , a team that has struggled to hit its customary heights over the last three seasons, failing to make the playoffs each time.After Stephen Fleming’s exit as CSK coach, there was considerable speculation over his successor. The management left the decision largely to Dhoni. Several names were discussed, including Hemang Badani, but one understands that the former captain’s comfort level with Zaheer was among the key factors behind the former left-arm pacer landing the job.Dhoni, as captain, had famously referred to Zaheer as the Sachin Tendulkar of bowling during India’s difficult 2012 World T20 campaign in Sri Lanka.“Dhoni obviously plays a key role in our decision-making process. He, along with captain Ruturaj Gaikwad and other members of the cricket committee, concluded that Zaheer is the best man for the job,” CSK managing director Kasi Viswanathan told TOI.CSK have struggled with their pace bowling lately, particularly at the death, and Zaheer’s mastery of reverse swing also worked in his favour.“Zaheer was a world-class bowler and has mentored many young cricketers, especially fast bowlers, over the years. Puducherry: Former Australia Test captain Tim Paine is currently working with Australia A, who will take on India A in the first four-day game in Puducherry starting Tuesday. With Australia preparing for the next Border-Gavaskar Trophy (Jan-Mar 2027), Paine spoke to TOI about the importance of exposing young players to Indian conditions, the next generation of Australian bowlers and his memories of facing Cheteshwar Pujara and Rishabh Pant Very important. That’s why we’re investing quite a lot of time and resources into getting the next group of cricketers over here, whether it’s through Australia A, the MRF Foundation or some of the work we do with younger players. The Border-Gavaskar Trophy is a really important one for us. It’s been more than 20 years since we’ve won it in India. The more times we can get here, acclimatise to the weather, food and different batting and bowling conditions and develop game plans, the better.We want to see how our players adapt to them. There’s a lot of footage available, but if it was as simple as saying, ‘This is his weakness and this is how you get him out’, they wouldn’t be the player they are now. It’s an amazing experience for our young bowlers to bowl to players of that quality in these conditions.(Cheteshwar) Pujara. He was hard to get out. He had great concentration and discipline and was tough. He used to irritate us. We were just trying to get him out. Pat Cummins eventually figured him out a bit and got him caught behind.I loved the way he came to Australia and played, how aggressive and confident he was. That’s something we’re trying to instil in this young group, the belief that you can go out and change games. That’s what Rishabh did against high-class bowlers. He threw them off their lines and lengths and put them under pressure. It was a great way to play, and a lot of the time I try and encourage our players to do the same thing.I haven’t watched enough of his white-ball cricket to say. I know his IPL over the last couple of years hasn’t been brilliant, but if he’s playing well, he could be playing in most white-ball teams around the world. It’s probably about capturing that form again and taking his red-ball cricket into white-ball cricket. There’s no reason why someone as skilled and talented as him, if he’s playing well, wouldn’t be a fantastic white-ball player.I think Australia have a good chance. Batting-wise, we probably haven’t scored as many runs as we would have liked in the last couple of summers, but there are still some high-quality players in the team. Either way, Australia will be very well prepared and I can’t see any reason why the Aussies can’t win.

NEW DELHI: There has been much intrigue around the head coach position at Chennai Super Kings ever since the franchise ended its long-term association with Stephen Fleming . The leadership group, under owner Rupa Gurunath, was keen on having an Indian-led support staff, but conversations with multiple candidates didn't materialise due to the lack of a "long-term vision".As first reported by TimesofIndia.com, Hemang Badani was the front-runner to take over the reins from Fleming , but a short contract and a smaller portfolio, only CSK and no overseas team, ended the conversations.CSK were unwilling to offer a long contract, and both Badani and another former India cricketer in the race felt it wasn't right to run a team they hadn't assembled and then be judged on it. Hemang Badani checked all the boxes, and negotiations were even in the final stages regarding money and contract duration. But he was initially given the impression that he would operate across at least three of the franchise's teams. Albie Morkel's appointment as the head coach of Joburg Super Kings in SA20 derailed the conversations with Badani; the contract duration was the real deal-breaker," says a source tracking developments.CSK insisted on operating on a year-by-year model, while the coaches in conversation wanted at least two years with the side to have a fair shot at setting things in order. Zaheer Khan 's appointment has surprised those tracking developments, and an industry insider feels this could at best be a stop-gap solution before the team presses reset during the mega auction."It's not a secret anymore that MS Dhoni is calling the shots with Rupa Gurunath. The way conversations ended with Badani, one more India cricketer and even an overseas candidate makes it clear the franchise is not yet willing to think long-term. Additionally, all these contracts are cyclic in nature. Mega auction to mega auction with an option to extend, of course," explains the source.While the exact details of the contract duration and compensation are not out yet, the price bracket CSK were operating around is understood to be between Rs 5 and 7 crore. We reached out to CSK Managing Director KS Viswanathan for details on the contract, and the story will be updated the moment he responds.Zaheer has served in different capacities at Mumbai Indians and Lucknow Super Giants in the past, and his exit from both setups was not under ideal circumstances. This will be his third role with an IPL team.Speaking on his appointment, Zaheer was quoted as saying by CSK: "It's an honour to be a part of one of the most successful teams in the history of the IPL. As a cricketer, I have faced CSK on the field and have thoroughly enjoyed the contests. The atmosphere created by the Superfans at Chepauk makes it even more special. I can't wait to join the legacy franchise with such a rich history."Rupa welcomed Zaheer into the setup and highlighted his ability to nurture young talent: "We are pleased to confirm Zaheer Khan as the Head Coach for Chennai Super Kings. Zaheer's distinguished playing career and proven ability to nurture young talent make him a valuable addition to our setup. We are confident that his guidance will help strengthen the core of this franchise."Zaheer last played in the IPL in 2017, ending his illustrious career with 102 wickets from 100 matches.

The Sports Authority of India (SAI) has rolled out a series of logistical and operational support measures for the Indian contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games, aiming to ensure athletes can focus on competition throughout the Games.Working alongside the Indian Olympic Association (IOA), the Embassy of India in Japan and the Games Organising Committee, SAI has stationed a dedicated reception and assistance team at the airport to welcome athletes, coaches and support staff arriving in Japan. At the onset of the Games, Indian diaspora had also stepped in to come to the assistance of the athletes if required.The team is assisting the contingent with immigration and arrival formalities, providing refreshments and guiding members to their accommodation and competition venues.Among the key initiatives is dedicated transport for India's shooting squad, with vehicles arranged to ferry athletes to and from competition venues. SAI has also deployed cars for medical personnel, allowing them to move quickly between venues and provide timely assistance to athletes.To address accommodation constraints, the organisation has secured additional rooms for coaches and support staff who could not be housed by the Games organisers because of limited availability.Double Asian Games 2026 medallist Rudrankksh Patil had spoken about accommodation issues he and his other shooting contingent faced in Aichi-Nagoya.Patil highlighted that the contingent had to wait for hours for their bus to arrive at the airport, and then the coaches had a disagreement with the hotel staff after they were not offered the hotel they booked their rooms in."We went to the welcoming centre. It took us three hours to wait for the bus over there. At 2 or 3 am, we started leaving for the hotel and reached there at around 3:30 or 4 am. After reaching the hotel, we realised that the hotel we had booked was not our hotel, we only had a couple of rooms over there, and that was supposed to be the best hotel," said Patil."And our coaches were fighting over there that if you can give us the confirmation for the best hotel, then how are you shifting us to some other hotel?" he added.The coordinated support forms part of SAI's efforts to provide seamless logistical, medical and operational assistance at the continental showpiece in Japan.
Article Summary: The Sports Authority of India (SAI) has rolled out a series of logistical and operational support measures for the Indian contingent at the Aichi-Nagoya 2026 Asian Games. SAI has stationed a dedicated reception and assistance team at the airport to welcome athletes, coaches and support staff arriving in Japan.

Article Title: Japan break Indian hearts as PV Sindhu, Unnati Hooda and Tanvi Sharma lose in Asian Games quarterfinal
Article Text:
India's PV Sindhu (ANI Photo)

Sindhu fights back before Yamaguchi takes control

Miyazaki puts Japan in command

Treesa-Gayatri keep India alive

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Okuhara seals Japan's place in semis

India's women's badminton team bowed out of the Asian Games after Japan secured a 3-1 victory in the quarterfinals on Tuesday, with the singles players unable to match the impact of the country's World Championships bronze-winning doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand.India were handed a difficult start when two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu took on world No.3 Akane Yamaguchi in the opening singles. Sindhu fought hard and took the first game 23-21, but Yamaguchi gradually took control of the contest to win the next two games 21-18, 21-6.Sindhu trailed 13-17 in the opening game but produced a strong recovery to move ahead. The contest featured several long rallies, with exchanges often stretching to 35-36 shots.The Indian had a game point but a wrong judgement on a back-line call gave Yamaguchi an opportunity to stay in contention. Sindhu earned another game point after Yamaguchi found the net and then finished the game with a cross-court forehand winner.Yamaguchi responded after the change of ends, establishing a two-point advantage at the mid-game interval. Sindhu again attempted to fight back after falling 12-17 behind, but the Japanese shuttler held firm to take the second game 21-18.The deciding game proved one-sided. Yamaguchi opened up a 14-6 lead and went on to earn 10 match points before sealing victory with a precise return.India needed Unnati Hooda to level the tie, but the youngster was unable to overcome 2022 world junior champion and current world No.7 Tomoka Miyazaki.Miyazaki controlled the contest to secure a 21-16, 21-18 victory, leaving Japan just one win away from the semifinals and putting India 0-2 behind.India's World Championships bronze-winning duo of Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand then delivered when the team needed them most.Fresh from winning their maiden World Championships bronze in New Delhi, Treesa and Gayatri defeated Yuki Fukushima and Mayu Matsumoto 21-17, 21-16 in the first doubles match.The victory reduced the deficit to 1-2 and briefly kept India's hopes of completing a comeback alive.The decisive match, however, went Japan's way.Young Indian shuttler Tanvi Sharma faced former world champion Nozomi Okuhara but could not find a response to her opponent's game. Okuhara won 21-12, 21-10 to give Japan an unassailable 3-1 lead.The result brought India's women's badminton team campaign at the Asian Games to an end, despite the strong showing from Treesa and Gayatri and Sindhu's spirited opening-game fight against Yamaguchi.
Article Summary: India's women's badminton team bowed out of the Asian Games after Japan secured a 3-1 victory in the quarterfinals on Tuesday. India were handed a difficult start when two-time Olympic medallist PV Sindhu took on world No.3 Akane Yamaguchi in the opening singles. India's World Championships bronze-winning doubles pair Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand kept India alive.

Article Title: India edge Thailand in thriller to reach Asian Games women’s team TT quarterfinals
Article Text:
Sreeja Akula

India overcame a major scare before defeating Thailand 3-2 in a dramatic women's team table tennis Round of 16 encounter at the Asian Games 2026 on Tuesday. Sreeja Akula held her nerve in the deciding match to send India into the quarterfinals, where they will face North Korea.The tie could hardly have started worse for India. Sreeja was two games ahead against Orawan Paranang but could not finish the job. Paranang fought back to win 7-11, 1-11, 11-9, 11-6, 12-10 and put Thailand in front.Yashaswini Ghorpade restored parity with a gritty 3-2 win over Suthasini Sawettabut. After taking the opening game 11-8, Yashaswini lost the next two 5-11, 7-11. She responded strongly, claiming the fourth and fifth games 11-9, 11-9 to make it 1-1.Thailand moved ahead again after Diya Chitale suffered a narrow defeat to Jinnapan Sawettabut. Chitale had a match point at 10-9 in the deciding game, but Jinnapan held her nerve to win 13-11. The Thai player prevailed 11-7, 5-11, 11-7, 11-7, 13-11.With India staring at elimination at 1-2, Yashaswini produced one of the key performances of the tie. She brushed aside Paranang 11-5, 11-8, 11-9 in just 21 minutes to bring India level and force a decider.Sreeja was then entrusted with the responsibility of closing out the contest against Suthasini. She dropped the opening game 9-11 but immediately turned the match around, winning the next two 11-6, 12-10.Suthasini led 8-6 in the fourth game, but Sreeja responded with five points in a row to seize control. She eventually won the game 11-9 and completed a 9-11, 11-6, 12-10, 11-8 victory, sparking India's comeback win.India's campaign also featured mixed results across several disciplines on Tuesday.In boxing, Sakshi Chaudhary advanced after beating the Philippines' Aira Villegas in the women's 51kg Round of 32. India's men's kabaddi team also registered a commanding 63-31 victory over South Korea in Group A.Elavenil Valarivan and Parth Mane finished second in the 10m air rifle mixed team qualification in shooting but ended fourth in the final.In soft tennis, Jay Meena defeated Pakistan's Hussain Arain 4-0 in the men's singles Group D, while Aadhya Tiwari went down 1-4 to Thailand's Alisha Ziegler in the women's singles.Wushu saw Langlentombi Devi Hanjabam finish ninth in the women's Nanquan final. In men's individual foil, Sachin and Hemash Singh both finished fourth in their respective pools.In swimming, Aryan Nehra came fourth in the men's 1500m freestyle final B. India's 4x100m medley relay quartet of Rishabh Das, Akash Mani, Benediction Beniston and Dhanush Suresh finished seventh overall in the heats to qualify for the final.There were setbacks too. Chetan Bhatt lost the men's 84kg kumite bronze medal match, while Alisha Choudhary was beaten 1-6 by Indonesia's Cok Istri Agung Sanistyarani in the women's -55kg Round of 16.India also suffered a 0-3 defeat to Malaysia in the men's Team Regu competition in sepaktakraw. In equestrian dressage, Ashish Limaye finished 13th, Arjan Nagra 23rd and Fouaad Mirza 26th.
Article Summary: India overcame a major scare before defeating Thailand 3-2 in a dramatic women's team table tennis Round of 16 encounter. Sreeja Akula held her nerve in the deciding match to send India into the quarterfinals, where they will face North Korea. India's campaign also featured mixed results across several disciplines on Tuesday.

Article Title: From 0.3-point heartbreak to Asian Games bronze: Rudrankksh Patil’s road to redemption
Article Text:
India's silver medalist Himanshu Dhillon, left, and bronze medalist Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil (AP photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya: At the last Asian Games , Rudrankksh Patil missed the bronze by 0.3 points in the shoot-off. On Monday, the 22-year-old finally had his medal and a measure of redemption.The past few years have been a roller-coaster ride for the Thane shooter, with Monday’s bronze coming after a series of near-misses and disappointments.At the 2022 World Championships in Cairo, Patil secured a quota place for the Paris Olympics, but lost out in the selection trials to Sandeep Singh . In 2023, he did not get an opportunity to defend his world title either.Patil believes those disappointments and circumstances have taken a mental toll. In Monday’s 10m air rifle individual final, he led at the halfway stage before gradually slipping away. He admitted the problem was more mental than tactical.“I got a little excited, too excited to finish the shot. I could have been much more patient there and it could have been better,” he said.The bronze, while a relief, also brought back another disappointment. Despite becoming world champion, Patil has not received the Arjuna Award . He admitted the snub affected him deeply.“I’ve never said this openly before, but I was disappointed when the Arjuna Awards were announced. I cried.It was also funny because I have been world No. 1 twice, a world-record holder four times. I won the world championship, World Cups and Asian titles, yet...”“That said, my state has supported me a lot and I’ve also received a lot of support from the central government through schemes like TOPS,” Patil added.“But I know these things are not in my hands. The only thing I can do is win medals. But I really hope the country appreciates it in some or the other way,” he added.
Article Summary: Rudrankksh Patil won bronze in the 10m air rifle individual at the Asian Games. The 22-year-old missed out on the bronze by 0.3 points in the shoot-off. The Thane shooter has had a series of near-misses and disappointments.

Article Title: Asian Games: Just 700gm between Suchika Tariyal and spot in MMA final
Article Text:
Nagoya: India's Suchika Tariyal takes a victory lap with the tricolour after securing a bronze medal in the women's traditional 60kg mixed martial arts event at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan. (PTI Photo)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Nagoya: Suchika Tariyal did not lose her fight in the arena. She lost it on the weighing scale.In a dramatic finish to the traditional 60kg MMA semifinal, the 36-year-old Indian was tied with Singapore’s Hui Hoon Toon after the bout and the mandatory one-minute extra time. Two judges voted for the Singaporean, while one sided with Suchika.Unhappy with the verdict, Suchika and her team felt she had landed more punches and strikes. The Mixed Martial Arts Sports Federation of India president Nikhil Kunder then lodged a protest with the Asian federation, sending the contest into arbitration.“We had to pay a fee of $1,000 for the arbitration process. We get to choose three random judges, who go into a closed room and analyse the last round. They give their scores and, based on that, a decision is made. Even then, the match ended in a draw,” Kunder told TOI.The Singapore federation was then given two options: go for counter-arbitration, allowing them to choose three judges from the panel, or have the fighters weighed, with the lighter athlete at the morning weigh-in declared the winner.“They opted for the latter,” Kunder said.That left Suchika at a disadvantage. She was found to be 700gm heavier than her Singaporean opponent at the morning weigh-in and, under the sport’s Asian body rules, was eliminated from the final.Kunder said the Indian team was also unable to verify the weight themselves because the athletes were staying on the cruise ship.“The players are staying on the cruise ship, so we officials don’t have access to them. We didn’t get to see the weight and had to take what was told to us at face value,” he said.The decision left Suchika heartbroken.“She just wouldn’t stop crying. It was very difficult to console her. But we had to accept the situation,” Kunder said.Later, Suchika said, “I gave my 100%, and I don’t agree with the decision that went in her favour.”The medal was India’s first in the sport, which made its debut at this edition of the Games.
Article Summary: Suchika Tariyal wins bronze medal in women's traditional 60kg mixed martial arts event at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan. The 36-year-old Indian was tied with Singapore’s Hui Hoon Toon after the bout and the mandatory one-minute extra time. Two judges voted for the Singaporean, while one sided with Suchika.

Article Title: Savita becomes India’s most-capped woman player as hockey team crush Indonesia 17-1
Article Text:
India’s women’s hockey team thrashed Indonesia 17-1 for its second consecutive Pool B win, with Deepika Sehrawat, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal and Navneet Kaur scoring hat-tricks.

Savita

becomes most-capped player

Nagoya: The Indian women’s hockey team continued its relentless start to the Asian Games, cruising to another big win as it eyes a first gold at the Games since 1982.At the Gifu Prefectural Green Stadium on Monday, India routed Indonesia 17-1, following Sunday’s 19-0 demolition of Uzbekistan in the campaign opener. A similar outing is expected against Thailand on Wednesday before India face their first serious test against hosts Japan on Friday.Deepika opened the scoring in the eighth minute and went on to add two more goals. Rutuja Pisal and Navneet Kaur also scored three goals apiece, while Sunelita Toppo, Lalremsiami and Sakshi Rana contributed two each. Ishika and skipper Salima Tete were the other scorers as eight Indian players sounded the boards.The day also belonged to seasoned goalkeeper Savita, who became India’s most-capped woman player. Monday’s game was her 321st appearance for the national team, taking her past Vandana Katariya’s tally of 320.Savita, who made her Asian Games debut in Jakarta in 2018, is making her fourth and last appearance at the continental Games.While the one-sided wins have provided an ideal start, they also present a challenge of adapting quickly to a higher level of competition as the tournament progresses.“The difference in quality is just too big,” chief coach Sjoerd Marijne told TOI. “I think it will be the same against Thailand and then we have to be ready for Japan. I’ve told the girls, just stay in rhythm, keep working on your basic skills, get used to the pitch and play our game.”
Article Summary: India thrash Indonesia 17-1 for its second consecutive Pool B win. Deepika Sehrawat, Rutuja Dadaso Pisal and Navneet Kaur score hat-tricks. Savita becomes India’s most-capped woman player.

Article Title: From Odisha’s villages to the Asian Games: The stories behind India’s women’s rugby squad
Article Text:
(From left) Odisha players Sandhyarani Tudu, Dumuni Marndi, Nirmalya Rout and Mama Naik in Kolkata on Monday

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Kolkata: Odisha’s rugby pipeline continues to power the Indian women’s sevens programme, with four players from the state earning selection in the squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.Senior campaigner Dumuni Marndi (Mayurbhanj) will feature in her second Asian Games alongside Mama Naik (Keonjhar), Nirmalya Rout (Bargarh) and Sandhyarani Tudu (Baripada, Mayurbhanj).For Marndi, the selection marks another chapter in a journey that began in rural Mayurbhanj, where her sporting ambitions were initially met with resistance at home.“The last Asian Games was a huge learning experience. At that time, there were so many seniors around me that I could just focus on playing. Now there is more responsibility because I’m one of the senior players,” said the vice-captain.The quartet’s inclusion is the latest testament to Odisha’s enduring influence on Indian rugby, with Sandhyarani Tudu among a long line of players to emerge from the state’s thriving grassroots system. She took up the sport after coaches introduced rugby at her school and believes Odisha’s strong culture has been central to its success.“Rugby is doing very well in Odisha. We consistently win medals and our team bonding is very strong. That has helped many players come through,” said Sandhyarani, a fly-half known for her tackling, passing and game awareness.Former age-group captain Mama Naik has also emerged as one of India’s brightest forward prospects, while Nirmalya Rout adds leadership credentials after captaining Odisha to the 2026 senior nationals crown.But even as Odisha continues to produce national team regulars, the sport is spreading across newer regions as well. Bihar, for instance, has two players in the squad.One of them is Arti Kumari, who continues to draw inspiration from her elder brother Rahul Kumar, who died in an accident in 2020.“My brother was my biggest supporter. He always encouraged me to chase my dreams,” said Arti, who hails from Nawada.Fellow Bihar player Guriya Kumari, from Muzaffarpur, has overcome a very different challenge. The youngster battled back from an ACL injury that required two surgeries on the same leg.“There was a time when I thought I would never be able to play again,” Guriya recalled.However, she has put all that behind her and is focused on the Asiad, where India will play its Pool B opener against Hong Kong on Oct. 1 at Paloma Mizuho Rugby Stadium. India's remaining two pool games will be against defending champions China and Malaysia.While head coach Paul Delport expects a stern test at the Asian Games, he is taking confidence from India’s recent performance at Asia Rugby Emirates Sevens Series, where the team finished sixth after recording victories over UAE and Iran. India also had a preparatory camp in Thailand, where they played practice matches against the hosts and Sri Lanka.“The players have improved enormously, both physically and in terms of game understanding. Considering how few tournaments we’re able to play, the progress has been exceptional,” Delport said of the team that finished seventh in the last Asiad.The former South Africa international, however, insisted that the focus must remain on the process rather than the results. Rugby India president Rahul Bose also echoed that sentiment, arguing that progress in team sports often takes longer to become visible on the scoreboard.But with an eye on the 2032 Olympics, Bose reiterated the need to create a more professional ecosystem for players.“We have to make rugby fully professional. You cannot just have camps and send players home. Centres of excellence and year-round programmes are the way forward,” he said in Kolkata on Monday.While Bose hinted that some of those plans could begin taking shape in the coming months, the immediate focus remains the Asian Games for which the team departs on Friday.The squad: Shikha Yadav (C), Dumuni Marndi (VC), Amandeep Kaur, Arti Kumari, Bhumika Shukla, Vaishnavi Patil, Guriya Kumari, Kalyani Patil, Mama Naik, Nirmalya Rout, Sandhya Rai, Sandhyarani Tudu, Ujjwala Ghuge.
Article Summary: Odisha's rugby pipeline continues to power the Indian women's sevens programme. Four players from the state earn selection in the squad for the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. India will play its Pool B opener against Hong Kong on Oct. 1 at Paloma Mizuho Rugby Stadium.

Article Title: Asian Games chaos! Typhoon Dujuan disrupts equestrian event; India’s three-day schedule cut short
Article Text:
The area around a ramen restaurant is flooded by heavy rain as Typhoon Dujuan approaches, in Oamishirasato, Chiba Prefecture, Japan (Reuters)

New Delhi:

Typhoon Dujuan cast a shadow over the Asian Games on Monday, forcing organisers to postpone the opening day of the equestrian eventing competition at Tokyo Equestrian Park as a precaution against worsening weather.The dressage phase, involving India’s riders, was called off after organisers grew wary of heavy rain and strong winds that could make conditions unsafe. An Indian rider told TOI that the decision was taken as a safety measure and riders were asked to stay indoors before returning to their designated team hotel.The postponement has squeezed the three-day programme into two days. Dressage and cross-country will now be held on Tuesday, with jumping scheduled for Wednesday.While swimming and cycling continued largely unaffected in Tokyo city, the outdoor equestrian competition bore the brunt of the approaching storm.The Japan Meteorological Agency warned that Dujuan could bring intense rain, strong winds and flooding to eastern Japan. Heavy rain is expected to persist into Tuesday.Meanwhile, some Indian riders have raised concerns over communications from chef-de-equipe, Lt Col Sandeep Dewan.Riders alleged that while Dewan was attending official delegation meetings, information from those meetings was not being shared with them.They also said they were not consulted about attending the opening ceremony. Riders stressed that the order of go should first be discussed among athletes and the coach before being finalised and conveyed to the chef-de-equipe.The concerns come with India seeking to defend its dressage gold from the previous Asian Games, as the competition resumes amid challenging weather.
Article Summary: Dressage and cross-country will now be held on Tuesday, with jumping scheduled for Wednesday. Japan Meteorological Agency warned that Dujuan could bring intense rain, strong winds and flooding to eastern Japan. Some Indian riders have raised concerns over communications from chef-de-equipe, Lt Col Sandeep Dewan.

Article Title: World Cup-winning Spain coach Luis de la Fuente rewarded with four-year contract extension until 2032
Article Text:
Luis de la Fuente rewarded with four-year Spain contract extension after leading La Roja to World Cup glory/ Image: AP

De la Fuente will lead Spain into the 2030 World Cup

A run of three major international titles

Spain head coach Luis de la Fuente attends training session ahead of a FIFA World Cup round of 32 soccer match against Austria in Carson, Calif., Wednesday, July 1, 2026. (AP Photo/Andre Penner)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Spain return to action after World Cup triumph

Spain have extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract through 2032 after the 65-year-old coach led La Roja to the World Cup title this summer, extending a remarkable run of success since he took charge of the national team in 2022. His previous agreement was due to expire in 2028, but the new deal keeps him in charge through the next two European Championships and the 2030 World Cup.The extension was ratified by the Royal Spanish Football Federation (RFEF) board of directors on Monday, with the new agreement adding four years to De la Fuente’s previous contract.The RFEF confirmed that De la Fuente will remain Spain coach through the 2028 European Championship, the 2030 World Cup and the 2032 European Championship.Spain will co-host the 2030 World Cup alongside Morocco and Portugal, while the 2032 European Championship will be split between Italy and Türkiye.De la Fuente's previous contract had been scheduled to run until 2028, meaning the extension gives him responsibility for two of the most significant tournaments on Spain's upcoming calendar beyond the next European Championship.RFEF board chairman Rafael Louzan described the decision as recognition of De la Fuente's achievements with the national team and his long association with the federation.“We're talking about the most successful head coach in the history of the national team, and after fourteen years with us, this is something Luis de la Fuente deserves, a long-term future at the RFEF,” Louzan said.The RFEF also said in a statement that De la Fuente “will extend his contract through the next two European Championships, in 2028 and 2032, as well as the 2030 World Cup”.De la Fuente took charge of Spain at the end of 2022, replacing Luis Enrique after Spain were eliminated by Morocco in the round of 16 at the World Cup in Qatar.His tenure has since transformed Spain's results on the international stage, beginning with the UEFA Nations League title in 2023, followed by European Championship glory in 2024 and the 2026 World Cup title earlier this year.The World Cup victory gave Spain their second World Cup title, completing a run that has established De la Fuente as one of the most successful coaches in the country's history.Before replacing Luis Enrique at senior level, De la Fuente had already spent years working within the RFEF structure, coaching several of Spain's youth teams.He spent a decade working with the federation's youth sides, winning the European Under-19 Championship and European Under-21 Championship, as well as a silver medal at the 2020 Olympic Games in Japan.His promotion to the senior team therefore followed an extended period working with Spanish players at international youth level rather than representing his first role within the federation.Spain will return to international action this week for the first time since beating Argentina in the World Cup final in New Jersey in July.Their first match comes against England at Wembley on September 26, beginning an extended international window that includes four UEFA Nations League fixtures.Spain will then return home to face Croatia in Seville on September 29, before hosting the Czech Republic in Oviedo on October 3.They will finish the international window with another trip to Croatia on October 6.The fixtures will mark De la Fuente's first games since guiding Spain to the World Cup title, while his new contract ensures that the coach who delivered the country's latest major trophies will remain responsible for the national team's next stage through 2032.
Article Summary: Luis de la Fuente has been rewarded with a four-year contract extension. The 65-year-old led Spain to the World Cup title in New Jersey in July. His previous contract was due to expire in 2028, but he will remain in charge through the next two European Championships and the 2030 World Cup.

Article Title: 'They're the best team in the league': Atlético boss Diego Simeone admits Barcelona are even better than his own side
Article Text:
Atlético Boss Diego Simeone Declares Barcelona La Liga's Best Team/ Image: AP

Simeone: Barcelona look like they are playing a different sport

Barcelona's Raphinha, right, celebrates with Lamine Yamal after scoring his side's second goal the Spanish La Liga soccer match between Sevilla and Barcelona in Seville, Spain, Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026. (AP Photo/Jose Breton)

Raphinha and Yamal are driving Barcelona's attack

Barcelona have opened a five-point lead over Atlético

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Diego Simeone was left impressed by Barcelona's start to the 2026/27 La Liga season after watching his Atlético Madrid side beat Real Madrid 2-1 in Sunday's Madrid derby. Hansi Flick's team have won all seven league matches so far, scored 31 goals and opened a five-point lead over Atlético at the top of the table, prompting Simeone to describe Barcelona as a team operating at a level that feels completely different from the rest of the league.Simeone was asked about Barcelona after Atlético's victory over Real Madrid and gave an emphatic assessment of the reigning champions' performances.“Honestly, they play amazingly well. It's like they're playing a different sport—a sport completely different from the one we play,” Simeone told ESPN.Barcelona have made a perfect start to their title defence, with their latest victory coming against Sevilla on September 19. Flick's side won 3-1 at the Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán Stadium, with Raphinha scoring a hat-trick after Youssouf Fofana had given the hosts an early lead.Simeone was particularly struck by Barcelona's attacking output and the way they have adapted without a traditional central striker leading the line.“They didn't really have a number nine, but then Raphinha stepped up, and he's got 12 goals in seven games. I think Yamal has seven, if I'm not mistaken,” he said.Raphinha's form has also put him at the top of the La Liga scoring charts, with the Brazilian five goals clear of Lamine Yamal, Kylian Mbappé and Sergio Camello in the race for the Pichichi.Raphinha has been central to Barcelona's explosive start, particularly after being used in a more central attacking role.Against Sevilla, he scored in the 22nd, 52nd and 69th minutes to complete his hat-trick and maintain Barcelona's unbeaten record, while Yamal has also contributed seven goals.The Atlético manager's comments also reflected his admiration for Barcelona's approach when they do not have possession.“The numbers are incredible; they press you high up the pitch, they close down your time on the ball, and they aren't afraid to take risks—even if it means conceding—because it seems like conceding a goal just makes them even more dangerous, since they're simply the better side,” Simeone said.That aggressive approach has been a defining part of Barcelona's opening seven matches, with the team combining their attacking production with pressure high up the pitch and a willingness to take risks.Simeone ultimately described Flick's side as the team setting the standard in the league.“Right now, they are the best team in the league, based on what they are showing,” he said.Barcelona's perfect record has left them five points clear of second-placed Atlético Madrid, who moved further into the title race by beating city rivals Real Madrid 2-1 on Sunday.The result leaves Atlético competing with Real Madrid and the other leading sides while Barcelona remain the only team with a perfect seven-game record at the top.Barcelona's next league match is scheduled for October 10 against Getafe, following the extended FIFA international break, with the game set to take place at Spotify Camp Nou.Barcelona and Atlético Madrid are then scheduled to meet on November 8, 2026, at the Riyadh Air Metropolitano in Madrid, giving Simeone's side their next direct meeting with the league leaders.
Article Summary: Diego Simeone impressed by Barcelona's start to La Liga 2026/27 season. Barcelona have won all seven league matches so far, scoring 31 goals. Raphinha has scored 12 goals in seven games, while Lamine Yamal has also scored seven.

Article Title: Who was Rijohn Jose? 29-year-old footballer dies in road accident in Kozhikode

Who was Rijohn Jose?

Calicut FC footballer Rijohn Jose died in a road accident in Kozhikode late Sunday night, days before the start of the new Super League Kerala season.The 29-year-old was travelling on a motorcycle with fellow footballer Ghani Ahmed Nigam when their vehicle collided with another motorcycle near Christian College on the Gandhi Road flyover at around 10.30 pm, news agency ANI reported.Both players were taken to Kozhikode Medical College Hospital after the accident. Rijohn died from his injuries at around 12.15 am IST. He was a native of Thrissur.Nigam, who also represents Kerala in the Santosh Trophy, suffered serious injuries and is undergoing treatment.The accident happened just hours after Calicut FC announced its squad for the upcoming Super League Kerala season. The team had also begun preparations for the tournament, which starts on September 25.Both Rijohn and Nigam had reached the city as part of the club's preparations.Rijohn had played as a defender for Forca Kochi in the previous edition of the Super League Kerala before returning to Calicut FC for the 2026 season.Gokulam Kerala FC on Monday expressed condolences over Rijohn's death.In a post on Instagram, the club extended its support to Rijohn's family, teammates and Calicut FC."It is with deep sorrow that we mourn the passing of Rijohn Jose of Calicut FC.Our heartfelt condolences to his family, teammates, friends, and the entire Calicut FC family. May they find strength and comfort in this difficult time," the club wrote."You left too soon. We weren’t ready for a goodbye. We weren’t ready to lose you, Rijohn. Holding your family, friends, teammates and everyone dear to you close in our thoughts. Forever, our champion. Rest in peace, Rijohn," Calicut FC said in a post on Instagram.Born in September 1997 in Thrissur, Rijohn Jose was a familiar name in Kerala football and had represented several clubs in domestic football.He began his professional career with FC Deccan before playing for Wayanad United, Sreebhumi FC and George Telegraph SC.He later became a regular defender for Forca Kochi FC in the 2024 and 2025 editions of the Super League Kerala.Ahead of the 2026 season, Rijohn returned to Calicut FC, the club he had helped win the inaugural Super League Kerala title in 2024 after defeating Forca Kochi FC 2-1 in the final.
Article Summary: Calicut FC footballer Rijohn Jose died in a road accident in Kozhikode late Sunday night. The 29-year-old was travelling on a motorcycle with fellow footballer Ghani Ahmed Nigam. Their vehicle collided with another motorcycle near Christian College on the Gandhi Road flyover at around 10.30 pm.

Article Title: Fake Covid-19 vaccination certificates? Former Arsenal star Granit Xhaka under investigation
Article Text:
Granit Xhaka (AP Photo)

Xhaka to be questioned in October
